description.narrative: (West Bank and Gaza): As is true of most economies in the Middle East, access to finance is a constraint for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in the West Bank. This constraint may limit SMEs' ability to purchase raw materials, hire new staff, purchase needed inputs, or expand existing operations. The Development Credit Authority (DCA) provides a partial guarantee mechanism that can mobilize needed funds in low-risk environments enabling borrowers to expand and grow. In FY 2014, USAID will use $300,000 of FY 2014 ESF funds to develop a 50 percent DCA guarantee to generate SME financing to meet needed specific constraints. This mechanism would have three basic components. First, a new movable collateral registry is being implemented in the West Bank. Coupled with the creation of a new law, leasing is now possible. Inchoate leasing companies are beginning to take off, but perceive risks as high given the undeveloped nature of the leasing sector. A partial guarantee can provide these first-movers with the comfort they need to establish and grow their leasing businesses, which will enhance access to leasing equipment for businesses. Second, trade financing for small operations that have new orders, i.e. purchase order finance, is also a growth opportunity. In purchase order finance, a business borrows against an order from a buyer, and the subsequent loan allows that business to purchase the necessary raw materials. A partial guarantee can support banks' provision of these new financing mechanisms. Third, a 50 percent guarantee on SME loans, broadly defined, may also be helpful to the business community. The guarantee will provide first-movers in the leasing sector with the comfort they need to establish and grow their leasing businesses, which will enhance access to productive assets.

(West Bank and Gaza): USAID will work on expanding the wastewater collection system in Tulkarem, a city of 73,000 in the West Bank. This includes expanding lines and upgrading the Irtah pump station to facilitate the treatment of wastewater being pumped into Israel. The activity will mitigate environmental pollution, protect the underground water against contamination, and limit the spread of water-borne diseases. Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. description.narrative: Launched in 2007, the Model Schools Network (MSN) Program is a USAID-funded initiative that aims to build institutional capacity in the Palestinian school system. The MSN Program is focused on developing a school improvement network that will serve as a model for basic education in Palestine. In its initial phase, the program supported 17 private schools in the West Bank. A second phase, begun in the fall 2009, includes an additional 40 public schools. The second phase, which is expected to end in September 2012, also provides local student scholarships and a range of in-service teacher training initiatives for 12 private schools in Gaza. The MSN Program is implemented in the West Bank and Gaza in partnership with the Palestinian Ministry of Education and Higher Education (MoEHE) and a dozen other organizations and institutions based in Palestine and the United States.

description.narrative: (West Bank and Gaza): This project aims to build the capacity of civil society organizations (CSOs) to play a more effective role in civic participation while focusing on the following areas:-Technical assistance to CSOs to adopt internal democratic management practices-Empowerment of youth and women skills and knowledge how to participate and respond to their community's needs.-Building the capacity of CSOs to respond to humanitarian crisis.~-Raising community awareness in general and of youth in particular on issues related to community issues and needs.-Empowering disabled people to find windows of opportunities to be better integrated in their local communities.

(West Bank and Gaza): The Youth Entrepreneurship Development Program (YED) strengthens the capacity of local Youth Serving Institutions (YSIs) including both youth serving NGOs and universities. USAID will use $1 million of FY~2014 funds to build the institutional capacity of these YSIs and provide support for the implementation of programs to develop youth employability and entrepreneurship skills. The YED project aims to serve youth ages 14-29 by implementing three project components: 1) build the capacity of YSIs, 2) support programs for employment, civic education and community service, and 3) provide internship opportunities for practical on-the-job training. YED will also form a consortium of YSIs with formal education establishments, and private sector companies to enhance networking for program delivery, promote best practices, and strengthen public-private partnerships with U.S and local firms. The YED project will contribute to the West Bank and Gaza Mission's goals by providing youth with skills needed for the job market, and enabling them to participate positively in addressing the socio-economic development challenges in their lives and their communities. The YED results will include: 1) providing internship opportunities for more than 500 youth graduates to gain valuable work experience, expand their technical knowledge, and improve their networking skills; 2) providing the opportunity for more than 1,000 youth to enhance their skills in community development research, leadership, and social innovation; 3) supporting career counseling and job fairs for more than 2,000 school and university students; and 4) building the capacity of at least 20 YSIs to incorporate best practices in employment, career counseling, entrepreneurial skills programs, and youth-led community initiatives.

(West Bank and Gaza): In FY 2014 USAID will invest $16,000,000 in the Palestinian Community Assistance Program (PCAP) to: 1) support economic recovery and development in Gaza through the creation of income generation and business development opportunities; and 2) address social recovery needs through improvements in education and health. The primary project components of PCAP include: (1) promoting food security and economic growth through home garden production, Information and Communication Technology (ICT) enterprise development, and skills training; and (2) maintaining social cohesion and recovery through community outreach programs focused on mental well-being, childhood education, humanitarian assistance, and cash-for-work programs. Key results expected under PCAP in FY 2014 include: provision of social assistance and services to 105,967 people in Gaza including 49,348 women, creation of 116,436 workdays of employment, 3,570 children participating in accelerated learning and after school programs and another 3,520 children receiving emotional well-being support, more than 4,125 individuals trained in improved agricultural production techniques, and 110 internships provided to fresh graduates.

(West Bank and Gaza): The Local Government and Infrastructure Program (LGI) is a program that aims to improve local governance and provide the basic infrastructure necessary for sustainable improvements in the quality of life for Palestinians. The program will strengthen local government capacity to respond effectively and efficiently to community needs by supporting capacity building, institutional development and service delivery skill enhancement initiatives. Governance activities will include promoting and institutionalizing good governance practices; encouraging public involvement through participatory governance mechanisms; and enhancing the capacity of the Ministry of Local Government to assume regulatory, policy development and strategic planning responsibilities. Over the life of the program, nearly 147 infrastructure projects will be completed under LGI to benefit over half a million Palestinians. In FY 2014, LGI will direct $15.98 million out of FY 2014 ESF to support the Palestinian Authority's High Impact Micro-Infrastructure Initiative (HIMII). HIMII projects will create jobs and fund infrastructure projects throughout the West Bank including the construction and repair of health clinics, roads, water systems, community centers, and schools. The HIMII is designed to show tangible benefits to the lives of Palestinians as peace negotiations advance and lay the groundwork for further economic growth. In addition, LGI will provide $3.5 million out of FY 2014 ESF funds in support of HIMII to strengthen the institutional and service delivery capacities of local governments; develop and institutionalize tools for citizen engagement in governance processes; strengthen local government capacity to respond to community infrastructure needs and manage sustainable government projects; and support national policy and regulatory reforms for the local governance sector. This program partially contributes to the Agency's education earmark.

description.narrative: (West Bank and Gaza): The Leadership and Teacher Development Project (LTD) focuses on: 1) Improving the capacity of schools to change classroom practices; 3) Enhancing policies within the Ministry of Education and Higher Education (MoEHE) to support in-service teacher development; 2) Establishing a national cadre of teacher educators and trainers; and, 4) Improving pre-service teacher education in Gaza. FY 2015 funds will be used to connect 68 schools to the Internet; train about 500 teachers and 68 principals; organize four regional conferences for participating teachers; and organize two study tours to countries in the region. Over the life of the project, the LTD aims to train 2,500 teachers, 300 principals, and about 200 staff members at the district level; improve the performance of training institutes; and improve the quality of pre-service teacher preparation programs at Al Azhar University in Gaza. These efforts emphasize the implementation of student-centered approaches to teaching and learning, collaborative educational leadership, and policy making. This program contributes to the Basic Education earmark and received full exception from implementing the Agency's Education Strategy.

title.narrative: Masters of Arts in Teaching Program (MAT)

description.narrative: (West Bank and Gaza): The Master of Arts in Teaching Program (MAT) aims to serve as a model for graduate-level in-service teacher training through a partnership between a local and a U.S. university. The program aims to introduce student-centered approaches in the classroom through enhancing the knowledge and practice of in-service teachers.FY 2015 funds will be used to award 54 two-year scholarships for in-service school teachers and supervisors to study at the MAT Program in order to create a core of educators who can lead education reform throughout the West Bank. Graduates of the MAT program are already assuming leadership roles within the MoEHE as senior teachers and supervisors who advocate improved teaching and learning practices in schools. Bard College is building the capacity of Al Quds University to ultimately take over the MAT program and sustain it. The MAT Program contributes to the long-term goal of the MoEHE of improving the quality of basic education. Over the life of the project, the MAT program will award 310 scholarships for in-service teachers and supervisors.This program contributes to the Basic Education earmark.

description.narrative: (West Bank and Gaza): The prime partner for this project is Augusta Victoria Hospital (AVH), using $435,318 in FY 2014 ESF funds, AVH plans to establish a new bone marrow transplantation and stem cell therapy program that serves West Bank and Gaza patients in East Jerusalem. The project is expected to reduce Palestinian Ministry of Health (MoH) burden of referring patients externally to Jordan or Israel and increasing local capacity to provide specialized health services.Nongovernmental organization (NGO) hospitals like AVH are an integral part of the Palestinian health care system. The Palestinian Authority's MoH relies heavily on NGO hospitals in the West Bank to provide essential secondary and tertiary care to Palestinians that the MoH is unable to provide.AVH, through its provision of specialty health care services, is committed to introducing services that are most commonly sought abroad, reduce overall health care costs, and increase the capacity of Palestinian providers to perform modern and innovative procedures. AVH currently has an on-going contract with the MoH to provide care and treatment for cancer patients. With prior year funding, the hospital is procuring the equipment needed to establish a bone marrow transplantation unit at AVH.Bone marrow transplantation services are not available within the Palestinian health system partially due to a lack of health professionals, especially nurses and allied health staff. With this funding hospital staff will be trained to perform their duties properly and in accordance with accreditation requirements and international standards.

title.narrative: Improving Eye Care Services for Palestinians

description.narrative: (West Bank and Gaza): Saint John is the main provider of eye care services in the West Bank and Gaza and has been providing its services for more than 129 years. St. John's project under this grant aims at improving eye health care in isolated areas of the West Bank by supporting a mobile outreach clinic that visits vulnerable localities to provide people with eye care services and performing corrective eye surgeries at their East Jerusalem Hospital to prevent blindness from cataracts. The project will also increase the capacity of the hospital group through the installation of an electronic Health Information System (HIS). The mobile outreach van is fully equipped with medical specialized equipment for screening patients suffering from a variety of eye diseases. The mobile clinic will examine and screen patients for eye diseases, provide primary eye care services and medications, and refer patients with complicated eye problems to one of Saint John's hospitals or clinics. Patients who suffer from cataracts will be referred to undergo corrective surgery. This project anticipates providing eye services to 27,000 to 30,000 marginalized Palestinians, performing 1,500 corrective surgeries, and installing a HIS for all four St. John's facilities during the total life of the award. These results will strengthen the delivery of health care services to the most vulnerable populations in the West Bank.With new incremental funding, this project will continue to provide eye care services through the mobile outreach clinic vulnerable localities in the West Bank, perform corrective eye surgery, and complete the final phase in HIS implementation.

(West Bank and Gaza): The PCID program aims to increase Palestinians' access to water, sanitation, and other basic infrastructure by implementing small and medium scale projects mainly in the rural and vulnerable communities. . .FY 2016 funds will be used to respond to urgent water, sanitation and other public infrastructure needs. The program will rehabilitate water systems to reduce water loss from inadequate networks; construct storm water drainage systems in Palestinian communities affected by flooding during the winter season; rehabilitate existing schools and construct new ones; and construct other small scale community infrastructure. . .Over the life of the project, 60 communities will have improved access to potable water supply, more than 20 communities will have access to improved sanitation systems, and more than 50 infrastructure projects will be constructed to serve other sectors. . .

description.narrative: (West Bank and Gaza): The Assistance to Vulnerable Groups Project (AVG) implemented by the United Nations World Food Program (UNWFP) works to mitigate food vulnerability provides essential humanitarian relief. In 2016, the United Nations estimated that 22.5% of the population in the West Bank and Gaza were food insecure, a modest improvement in food security compared to 27% in 2014. .With FY 2017 funds, the AVG project will support continued provision of high-quality food assistance to help meet basic food needs and improve dietary diversity of 186,500 beneficiaries in the West Bank and Gaza, 95,000 of whom are in Gaza and 41,500 are in the West Bank. description.narrative: (West Bank and Gaza): The Rubble Removal Project removes rubble and debris created during the seven week military operation in Gaza during the summer of 2014. These efforts will facilitate work by the Palestinian Water Authority and Coastal Municipalities Water Utility to repair infrastructure buried beneath the rubble and restore and sustain essential water and sanitation services. description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. The first component of the USAID supported program aims to improve coordination, policy planning, and strategic development within the justice sector, as well as provide modern IT equipment and capabilities. The second part of NETHAM focuses on the enforcement of laws and court decisions, which is considered to be problematic within the Palestinian judicial system. description.narrative: The Civic Engagement Program II (CEP II) project seeks to engage and promote moderate voices in the West Bank and Gaza (WB/G) to further the prospect for peaceful political solutions and economic development. In addition, the program will provide capacity building support to a range of institutions in the WB/G. This contract is considered a follow-on that continues programming to bolster prospects for peace in the region undertaken from June 2005 until September 2008 under USAIDs Office of Transition Initiatives (OTI) and CEP I respectively. CEP II is an established in-kind grant mechanism that maintains a rapid and flexible response capacity to emerging needs; continues well-established working relationships with key Palestinian Authority (PA) figures; advances working linkages with key moderate leaders, including political leadership at the national and local levels as well as civic leaders; and preserves strong analytical capabilities related to the political environment and windows of opportunity for programming a wide spectrum of functional and geographic areas.

Using short-term interventions, PACE builds the capacity and improves citizen services with five principle ministry partners: Ministry of Finance (MOF), Ministry of Transportation (MOT), Ministry of Public Works and Housing (MOPWH), Ministry of Telecommunication and Information Technology (MTIT), and Ministry of Interior (MOI) Civil Affairs Directorate.

description.narrative: The EDIP Project was a three-year program devoted to accelerating investment in Palestinian economic sectors that foster rapid economic growth and the creation of around 500,000 jobs to accomodate the unemployed and new entrants to the labor market. The EDIP approach was structured to leverage USAID resources in stimulating private investment that lead to new jobs, exports, sustainable market linkages, business support, and enabling services. EDIPs primary goals and strategic approach were to increase firm competitiveness by providing linkages to markets and technology and to strengthen Palestinian institutions and business-enabling environments by strategically addressing success factors defined by investors and firms as especially critical to the growth of specific value chains.

description.narrative: The Trade Facilitation Project, funded by USAID, stimulates trade in the West Bank and Gaza and facilitates cargo movement by supporting facility and equipment upgrades on the Palestinian side of selected cargo crossing points and operational efficiencies at Israeli-managed crossings. Through the project, Chemonics works with local traders and their associations to lower trade costs through improvements in packing, loading, logistics, and transportation, and by facilitating dialogue with the government of Israel to speed the movement of Palestinian cargo to markets in Israel and abroad.

The Investment Climate Improvement Project assisted the Palestinian Authority in adopting and implementing laws, regulations, policies, and procedures required to bring it into compliance with the multilateral trade framework of the World Trade Organization. The USAID Investment Climate Improvement Project had two components: policy reform and fiscal reform. The policy reform component had two sub-components: preparing the Palestinian Authority to achieve World Trade Organization observer status and improving the business enabling environment.
